title: Coronation Chicken
subtitle: Cold chicken in a curried mayonnaise with mango chutney and almonds
excerpt: Cold cooked chicken in a mild curry-spiced mayonnaise with mango chutney, sultanas, and flaked almonds. Created for the coronation of Elizabeth II in 1953, now a British buffet staple.
sourceNotes: Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume, The Constance Spry Cookery Book (1956), the original recipe was developed by Spry and Hume for the coronation banquet of Queen Elizabeth II in 1953. The original called for poulet reine Elizabeth; later versions substituted curry powder for the more complex spice blend. This version follows the simplified domestic standard.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale freely. The sauce can be made ahead and the chicken added an hour before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made 1 to 2 hours ahead and chilled so the flavours develop. Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

content.text: Coronation chicken is cold cooked chicken in a mildly spiced mayonnaise sauce with mango chutney, sultanas, and toasted almonds. It is one of the few dishes invented for a specific public occasion that became embedded in everyday British cooking. Use any cooked chicken: leftover roast, poached breast, or rotisserie. The sauce takes 5 minutes to mix.

items.prepNote: cooked and shredded, or leftover roast chicken

content.text: Mix {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise with {{curry-powder}} of mild curry powder, {{mango-chutney}} of mango chutney, and the juice of {{lemon}} in a large bowl. Stir until smooth.
Add {{sultanas}} of sultanas if using. Taste and adjust the seasoning: you may want a little more lemon juice or curry powder depending on the chutney.
Add {{chicken-breast}} of shredded cooked chicken and fold gently to coat. Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Before serving, scatter {{almonds-flaked}} of toasted flaked almonds over the top if using.

rows.cause: Chutney-heavy balance or too few acidic notes
rows.fix: Add more lemon juice and taste. A small pinch of salt also balances sweetness.

rows.symptom: Sauce is too thick and stodgy
rows.cause: Too much mayonnaise relative to chicken
rows.fix: Thin with a small spoon of natural yogurt or add more chicken to balance.
Use chicken cooked gently, or use thigh meat instead, which stays more tender through cooking.

rows.symptom: Curry flavour is raw and harsh
rows.cause: Curry powder not bloomed before adding
rows.fix: Toast the curry powder in a dry pan for 30 seconds before mixing into the mayonnaise. It softens the raw spice flavour.

content.text: Coronation chicken was created by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II in June 1953. It was served as poulet reine Elizabeth to 350 guests. The original used a complex spice blend with apricot and cream. The simpler version with curry powder and mayonnaise spread through home cooking in the following decades. It is now found at sandwich counters, supermarket deli sections, and buffet tables across the country.
